quiz.q: Why is the 74th Constitutional Amendment considered a half-hearted reform in urban governance?
options: It lacks an institution of direct democracy comparable to the rural Gram Sabha.
It transfers real municipal executive authority entirely from commissioners to mayors.
It strictly mandates five tiers of local government across all urban areas.
It abolishes the state government's power to create special purpose vehicles.
quiz.why: The 74th Amendment remains structurally weaker than the 73rd Amendment because it created no forum for direct democracy equivalent to the Gram Sabha.

quiz.q: According to Isher Judge Ahluwalia, why has the Smart Cities initiative faced slow progress?
options: Municipal councils possess excessive constitutional autonomy that stalls centrally funded infrastructure.
Governments bypass and neglect municipalities by relying heavily on Special Purpose Vehicles.
The 74th Amendment prohibited private capital investment within metropolitan municipal corporations.
Elected city mayors have usurped the administrative responsibilities of appointed municipal commissioners.
quiz.why: Isher Judge Ahluwalia highlights that smart city goals cannot succeed when governments neglect municipal bodies and rely instead on Special Purpose Vehicles.

quiz.q: What did empirical studies by the Ministry of Panchayati Raj highlight regarding women's reservation?
options: Women representatives permanently reinforced the patriarchal practice of proxy rule by husbands.
Elected women consistently prioritized industrial development over drinking water and rural sanitation.
Reservation produced psychological empowerment and encouraged families to send daughters to school.
Administrative performance deteriorated severely due to the absence of formal educational qualifications.
quiz.why: Studies by the Ministry showed that reservation challenged proxy rule, creating psychological empowerment and inspiring families to educate their daughters.

quiz.q: According to Rajni Kothari, which institutional factor led to the rise of grassroots micro-movements?
options: The rapid legislative expansion of direct democracy through local ward committees.
The complete financial independence of municipal corporations from state-level budgetary grants.
The constitutional prohibition on trade unions engaging in collective industrial bargaining.
Political parties abandoned their movement character and turned into mere electoral machines.
quiz.why: Rajni Kothari argued that grassroots micro-movements arose because mainstream political parties abandoned their movement orientation, reducing themselves to election machines.
